articles.summary: Halozyme Therapeutics, Inc. (Nasdaq: HALO) ("Halozyme" or the "Company") today confirmed that the Company expects zero to minimal royalty revenue impact based on its analysis of the final rule for the Medicare Drug Price Negotiation Program ("Program") issued by the U.S. Centers for Medicare Medicaid Services ("CMS") on November 5th, 2026. "Based on our analysis of CMS's final rule and the statutory framework established under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act ("OBBBA"), Halozyme projects zero to minimal impact to its royalty revenues through at least 2035. Importantly, there is also no projected impact on the Company's ability to execute new ENHANZE® partnership agreements where improving the patient treatment experience and competitive differentiation continue to be the top reasons ENHANZE is utilized," commented Dr. Helen Torley, President and Chief Executive Officer. articles.summary: Halozyme Therapeutics, Inc. (Nasdaq: HALO) (Halozyme), today provided an update on the German preliminary injunction hearing that overturned the decision issued in December 2025, ordering Merck to refrain from distributing and offering Keytruda SC in Germany. "We are disappointed that the Higher Regional Court overturned the preliminary injunction halting the launch of Keytruda SC in Germany. We disagree with the decision and will immediately file an infringement lawsuit against Merck in Germany seeking permanent relief, which is not precluded by today's decision," said Mark Snyder, Chief Legal Officer of Halozyme. articles.title: Halozyme Provides Update on German Preliminary Injunction Hearing

articles.summary: Halozyme Therapeutics, Inc. (Nasdaq: HALO) (Halozyme) today announced that Johnson Johnson was granted accelerated approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for RYBREVANT FASPRO™ (amivantamab and hyaluronidase-lpuj), which is co-formulated with ENHANZE®, as a single agent for the treatment of adults with recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) whose disease has progressed on or after platinum-based chemotherapy and an anti-PD-(L)1 antibody. The indication does not include patients with oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma that is HPV-associated. It is the first approval of a dual-targeted therapy in this setting, simultaneously targeting epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)- and mesenchymal-epithelial transition (MET). "This approval will further expand the reach of RYBREVANT FASPRO in a high unmet need population," said Dr. Helen Torley, President and Chief Executive Officer of Halozyme.
